evidence.title: ʿUbeidiya (Jordan Rift Valley): Earliest Levantine Acheulean & Villafranchian corridor
evidence.dateBasis: Biostratigraphy, palaeomagnetism and cosmogenic-burial age estimates of upturned Jordan Valley lake beds.
evidence.summary: Preserves early Out-of-Africa Acheulean large cutting tools, spheroids and scarce hominin elements along lakeshores of the central Jordan Rift.
evidence.limits: Tectonic tilting of the Rift beds leaves precise bed-by-bed radiometric constraints challenging.

evidence.title: Gesher Benot Yaʿaqov (Hula Basin, Upper Jordan): Early controlled fire & basalt cleavers
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetostratigraphic placement spanning the 780 ka Matuyama–Brunhes reversal with waterlogged plant, nut and wood remains.
evidence.summary: Waterlogged palaeo-Hula lakeside horizons reveal structured hearth clusters of burnt flint micro-artifacts, cracked nuts, processed fish and African-affinity basalt cleaver manufacture.
evidence.limits: No hominin cranial fossils have yet emerged to establish exact species assignment beyond African-derived Acheulean makers.

evidence.title: Qesem Cave (Samarian Hills): Acheulo-Yabrudian blade technology & central hearth
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series and ESR/TL dating of speleothems, burnt flints and fallow-deer teeth across a 300-ka-old central wood-ash hearth.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates habitual use of a large fixed hearth, fallow-deer meat sharing, systematic flint blade production and dental remains showing Levantine Middle Pleistocene variation prior to classic Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: Taxonomic attribution of Qesem teeth remains open among regional archaic Homo and early sapiens-clade models.

evidence.title: Tabun Cave & Nahal Meʾarot (Mount Carmel): Deep Lower-to-Middle Paleolithic master sequence
evidence.dateBasis: Post-IR IRSL (pIRIR290), ESR and TL chronologies spanning 25 metres of Lower Acheulean, Acheulo-Yabrudian and Levantine Mousterian stratigraphy.
evidence.summary: Provides the benchmark Levantine chronological column from Upper Acheulean handaxes through Tabun C1 Neanderthal-affiliated skeletal remains and bird/ungulate Mousterian subsistence.
evidence.limits: Diagenetic uranium uptake and historical Garrod-era trench mixing complicate fine sub-layer correlation for older finds.

evidence.title: Amud & Kebara Caves (Galilee & Carmel): Late Levantine Neanderthal burials & seasonality
evidence.dateBasis: TL/ESR dating paired with dental microwear and seasonal mortality analysis of gazelle and fallow deer.
evidence.summary: Kebara 2 (preserving the hyoid bone) and Amud Neanderthals practiced intentional cave burials, Levantine Mousterian Levallois flaking and multi-season hunting alongside shifting early modern human windows.
evidence.limits: Chronological overlap with adjacent early Homo sapiens dispersals remains tightly constrained at century–millennial resolution.

evidence.title: Manot Cave (Western Galilee): 55,000-year-old Homo sapiens cranium at the Eurasia threshold
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-thorium dating of stalagmite crusts sealing the Manot 1 calvaria and Ahmarian Aurignacian-linked cave chambers.
evidence.summary: Provides direct fossil evidence of a modern human population in the northern Levant at the exact moment major Non-African Homo sapiens–Neanderthal gene flow and Initial Upper Paleolithic dispersals unfolded.
evidence.limits: No ancient DNA has yet been extracted from the calcified Manot 1 partial cranium.

evidence.title: Ohalo II (Sea of Galilee): 23,000-year-old submerged LGM fisher-gatherer camp & wild cereals
evidence.dateBasis: Dozens of AMS radiocarbon dates on waterlogged brush-hut wood, twisted grass bedding and wild emmer/barley seeds.
evidence.summary: Preserved under anoxic lake silt during a drought exposure, six brush huts at Ohalo II yield grinding slabs, sickles and >140 wild plant taxa including wild emmer and barley long before Holocene domestication.
evidence.limits: Exposed only during extreme twentieth-century low-lake levels, limiting full shoreline perimeter sampling.

evidence.title: Shubayqa 1 & Natufian Levant (NE Jordan/Israel): Stone dwellings, bread & earliest sedentism
evidence.dateBasis: High-resolution AMS Bayesian sequences on Shubayqa 1 hearths paired with clay/bone ornament and wild cereal analyses across Eynan/Ein Mallaha and Hayonim.
evidence.summary: Late Epipaleolithic wetland foragers built circular basalt-walled houses, prepared leavened/unleavened flatbreads from wild tubers and cereals 4,000 years before farming, and crafted clay personal ornaments.
evidence.limits: Younger Dryas cooling triggered fluctuating mobility between semi-sedentary hamlets and desert camps.

evidence.title: Khall Amayshan 4 & Nefud Palaeolakes (Saudi Arabia): Five Green Arabia hominin dispersals
evidence.dateBasis: Single-grain OSL dating of five stacked interglacial palaeolake sediments bearing distinct Acheulean and Middle Paleolithic stone assemblages.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates that monsoon shifts repeatedly greened northern Arabia into grassland lake basins (~400, ~300, ~200, ~130–75 and ~55 ka), drawing successive Lower and Middle Paleolithic populations across the Saharo-Arabian belt.
evidence.limits: Arid deflated lake basins preserve stone tools and hippopotamus/elephant fauna but almost no human bone beyond Al Wusta.

evidence.title: Jebel Faya & Buhais Rockshelter (Sharjah, UAE): Multi-phase Pleistocene SE Arabian record
evidence.dateBasis: OSL luminescence dating of stratified Middle Paleolithic assemblages at Jebel Faya (MIS 7, MIS 5 and MIS 3) plus newly dated 60–16 ka horizons at Buhais.
evidence.summary: Shows recurring human occupation of southeastern Arabia between ~210 and 16 ka along the exposed Persian–Oman Gulf corridor using bifacial foliates and blade industries prior to late-glacial hyper-aridity.
evidence.limits: Acidic/calcareous cave geochemistry has not yielded human DNA or diagnostic Pleistocene crania at Jebel Faya.

evidence.title: Jubbah, Jebel Arnaan & Shuwaymis (Ha’il, Saudi Arabia): Terminal Pleistocene monumental rock art
evidence.dateBasis: Luminescence and uranium-series dating of ephemeral-playa sediments overlying fallen cliff blocks beneath life-sized wild camel and equids engravings.
evidence.summary: Reveals that hunter-foragers recolonized interior northern Arabia by ~12,800–11,400 years ago around seasonal playa lakes, carving monumental camel, ibex and equid panels high across desert cliff faces.
evidence.limits: Direct mineral-crust dates remain scarce compared with sediment-buried panel foundations.

evidence.title: Mezmaiskaya & Ortvale Klde (Caucasus): Two Neanderthal cultures & Upper Paleolithic turnover
evidence.dateBasis: Nuclear/mitochondrial aDNA from Mezmaiskaya Neanderthal infants plus ultrafine AMS radiocarbon across Greater and Lesser Caucasus rockshelters.
evidence.summary: Distinguishes Eastern Micoquian (North Caucasus) and Zagros-Levantine Mousterian (South Caucasus) Neanderthal groups separated by the Greater Caucasus ridge, showing genetic population turnover ~80 ka and complete Upper Paleolithic replacement by ~39–38 ka.
evidence.limits: Some older historical cave collections lack fine micromorphological charcoal context.

evidence.title: Qaleh Kurd Cave (Qazvin, Iranian Central Plateau): Middle Pleistocene hominin tooth & hunting camp
evidence.dateBasis: Electron spin resonance and uranium-series dating on horse teeth associated with an archaic Homo deciduous canine on the Iranian Plateau.
evidence.summary: Establishes the oldest securely dated stratified hominin fossil and Mousterian-like hunted equid assemblage on the Iranian Central Plateau east of the Zagros.
evidence.limits: A single deciduous tooth leaves fine species resolution between H. heidelbergensis and early Neanderthals open.

evidence.title: Shanidar, Warwasi & Yafteh Caves (Zagros, Iraq/Iran): Neanderthal burials & Baradostian blades
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/radiocarbon redating of newly excavated Shanidar Z articulated remains alongside Zagros Mousterian and Baradostian bladelet analyses.
evidence.summary: High-altitude Zagros caves preserve repeated Neanderthal funerary clustering (Shanidar 1–10 and Shanidar Z), trauma-care evidence, and the shift into early Upper Paleolithic Baradostian bladelet ornaments at Yafteh and Warwasi.
evidence.limits: Pollen cluster interpretations in older 1950s Shanidar soil samples are currently reassessed via bees/burrowing taphonomy.

evidence.title: Teshik-Tash Grotto & Obi-Rakhmat (Uzbekistan): Central Asian Neanderthal frontier
evidence.dateBasis: Mitochondrial DNA confirmation (Eastern Neanderthal clade) paired with technological lithic re-analysis of the Baisuntau mountain rock shelter.
evidence.summary: Yielded an 8–10-year-old Neanderthal child burial encircled by Siberian ibex horn cores, linking easternmost Classic Neanderthals genetically with the Altai foothills across Inner Asian mountain corridors.
evidence.limits: Excavated in 1938 before modern stratigraphic micro-dating, leaving exact burial sediment age anchored genetically and typologically.

evidence.title: Denisova Cave Stratigraphy (Altai Mountains, Siberia): Three-lineage Eurasian crossroads
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian OSL, uranium-series, sedimentary aDNA across 300 layers and radiocarbon dates on Main, East and South Gallery deposits.
evidence.summary: Captures 250,000 years of alternating Denisovan (~280–55 ka), Neanderthal (~190–90 ka and ~60 ka) and Initial Upper Paleolithic/bone-ornament occupation culminating around 45–30 ka.
evidence.limits: Attribution of personal ornaments at ~48–43 ka among late Denisovans vs incoming H. sapiens remains actively investigated.

evidence.title: Mal’ta & Buret’ (Angara Valley, Lake Baikal, Siberia): Ancient North Eurasian mammoth camps
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on MA-1 child genome, stone slab houses, carved ivory waterfowl/figurines and reindeer antler industries.
evidence.summary: Carved ivory female figurines, flying waterfowl pendants and the 24,000-year-old MA-1 Ancient North Eurasian genome link Late Ice Age Lake Baikal camps ancestrally to both later European steppe herders and First Americans.
evidence.limits: Multiple 1920s–1950s excavation campaigns varied in three-dimensional provenience recording.

evidence.title: Afontova Gora & Upper Yenisei Valley (Siberia): Post-LGM microblade hunters
evidence.dateBasis: Alluvial terrace radiocarbon dates, composite wedge-shaped microblade cores and Ancient North Eurasian (AG2/AG3) skeletal genomes.
evidence.summary: Illustrates cold-adapted wedge-shaped microblade and slotted-bone technology across open Yenisei steppe-tundra landscapes carrying Ancient North Eurasian genetic continuity to the Pleistocene–Holocene transition.
evidence.limits: River terrace erosion destroys portions of upper Pleistocene camp floors along the Yenisei.

evidence.title: Attirampakkam (Tamil Nadu, South India): 1.5 Ma Acheulean & early Middle Paleolithic shift
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic 26Al/10Be burial ages on Early Pleistocene Acheulean horizons paired with pIR-IRSL dates (385–172 ka) on Levallois Middle Paleolithic layers.
evidence.summary: Establishes one of Asia’s oldest securely dated Acheulean biface records by ~1.51 Ma, later transitioning in situ by ~385 ka to preferential Levallois points and blades without requiring sudden late population replacement.
evidence.limits: Fluvial ferricrete silt lacks preserved human skeletal remains at Attirampakkam.

evidence.title: Isampur Quarry (Hunsgi–Baichbal Basin, Karnataka): Limestone Acheulean workshop floor
evidence.dateBasis: Combined ESR on herbivore tooth enamel and bedrock-quarry stratigraphic context in the Deccan peninsula.
evidence.summary: Reveals an intact Early Pleistocene quarry workshop beside a palaeostream where hominins wedged limestone slabs into large Acheulean cleavers, handaxes and hammers.
evidence.limits: ESR age estimates on tooth enamel carry wider uncertainties than volcanic-tephra sites.

evidence.title: Hathnora (Central Narmada Valley, Madhya Pradesh): Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo calvaria
evidence.dateBasis: Boulder-conglomerate fauna, Acheulean bifaces and comparative morphology of the thick-vaulted Narmada cranial cap.
evidence.summary: South Asia’s sole confirmed pre-sapiens cranial vault blends archaic erectus-like wall thickness with expanded cranial capacity (~1,150–1,420 cc), reflecting Indian Middle Pleistocene archaic diversity.
evidence.limits: Fluvial boulder-bed deposition allows only broad Middle Pleistocene rather than single-horizon radiometric precision.

evidence.title: Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh): Acheulean to Late Pleistocene microliths
evidence.dateBasis: Multilayer sandstone-shelter stratigraphy from Late Acheulean bifaces through Middle Paleolithic scrapers, Upper Paleolithic blades and pre-Holocene rock paintings.
evidence.summary: Vindhyan quartzite shelters at Auditorium Cave and Shelter IIIF-23 document millennia of occupation continuity from Late Acheulean floor cupules and cleavers into modern-human microlithic foraging.
evidence.limits: Pre-ceramic mineral pigments on sandstone walls resist direct radiocarbon assay without organic binders.

evidence.title: Jwalapuram (Jurreru Valley, Andhra Pradesh): Middle Paleolithic across 74 ka Toba Ash
evidence.dateBasis: Primary and reworked 74 ka Youngest Toba Tuff tephra seals separating OSL-dated Middle Paleolithic stone tool layers above and below.
evidence.summary: Shows continuity of radial and blade-core Middle Paleolithic toolmaking across the 74,000-year Toba super-eruption ash fall, shifting later into ~35 ka backed microlithic industries.
evidence.limits: Without associated human fossils or aDNA, species identity beneath the Toba ash stays inferred from African–Asian tool comparisons.

evidence.title: Kitulgala Beli-lena & Batadomba-lena (Sri Lanka): 45 ka rainforest microliths & bone bows
evidence.dateBasis: Revised AMS/OSL chronologies on quartz geometric microliths, double-pointed bone/monkey-tooth projectile tips and arboreal primate/squirrel fauna.
evidence.summary: Reveals that Homo sapiens mastered dense tropical wet-zone rainforest canopy hunting using backed quartz microliths and bone-tipped projectiles outside Eurasia’s classic savanna biomes.
evidence.limits: No Late Pleistocene Sri Lankan nuclear genomes have yet been recovered due to humid tropical DNA degradation.

evidence.title: Shangchen (Lantian, Chinese Loess Plateau): 2.12 Ma–1.26 Ma Early Pleistocene artefacts
evidence.dateBasis: High-resolution loess–palaeosol magnetostratigraphy tied to Olduvai/Réunion subchrons across 17 stone-artefact horizons.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates repeated core, flake and hammerstone knapping on the southern Loess Plateau as early as 2.12 Ma, establishing that early Homo dispersed into temperate East Asia prior to Dmanisi.
evidence.limits: No hominin bones occur alongside the Shangchen stone tools, leaving exact species morphology uncertain.

evidence.title: Majuangou, Xiaochangliang & Nihewan Basin (Hebei, China): 1.66 Ma northern lake camps
evidence.dateBasis: Palaeomagnetic polarity sequences in lacustrine Nihewan beds bracketing Majuangou III, Shangshazui and Xiaochangliang.
evidence.summary: Documents high-latitude (40°N) Early Pleistocene lakeside foraging with butchered elephant/mammoth and equid bones plus bipolar and freehand small-flake technologies during interglacial phases.
evidence.limits: Northern basin deposits remain sparser during full glacial loess stages.

evidence.title: Yunxian (Quyuanhekou) & Gongwangling (Central China): 1.77–1.63 Ma Homo erectus crania
evidence.dateBasis: 26Al/10Be cosmogenic isochron burial dates (~1.77 Ma at Yunxian) alongside palaeomagnetic Gongwangling Lantian redating (~1.63 Ma) and enamel proteomics.
evidence.summary: Houses the oldest in-situ East Asian Homo erectus skulls (Yunxian 1–3 and Gongwangling), demonstrating early cranial diversity along the Qinling–Hanjiang ecotone.
evidence.limits: River-terrace tectonic deformation cracked Yunxian 1–2 prior to digital 3D restoration.

evidence.title: Zhoukoudian Locality 1 & Upper Cave (Beijing): Classic Peking Man to Upper Paleolithic
evidence.dateBasis: 26Al/10Be burial dating of Locality 1 (~770–400 ka), newly sequenced enamel proteomes and AMS radiocarbon dates on Upper Cave Homo sapiens burials.
evidence.summary: Locality 1 preserves over 40 Homo erectus individuals, bipolar quartz tools and Middle Pleistocene ash traces, crowned above by Upper Cave ochre-sprinkled H. sapiens burials, pierced shells and bone needles.
evidence.limits: Original pre-1941 Locality 1 crania disappeared in wartime transit; anatomical study relies on detailed Weidenreich casts and newer Locality 1/4 finds.

evidence.title: Hualongdong, Xuchang & Harbin (“Dragon Man”): Middle Pleistocene archaic diversity & proteomes
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series and sediment dating (~300 ka Hualongdong, >146 ka Harbin, ~125–105 ka Lingjing Xuchang) plus 2025 ancient proteome and mtDNA identification of Harbin as Denisovan-affiliated.
evidence.summary: Middle Pleistocene East Asian crania display striking mosaic combinations of large brains, archaic brow ridges and derived flatter faces, with the massive Harbin cranium linked by ancient proteins and dental-calculus mtDNA to Denisovans.
evidence.limits: Nuclear genome sequencing has not yet been completed across Hualongdong or Xuchang specimens.

evidence.title: Fuyan (Daoxian) & Zhirendong Caves (South China): Early subtropical Homo sapiens debates
evidence.dateLabel: c. 100,000–65,000 years ago (stratigraphic vs direct-AMS debate)
evidence.dateBasis: U-series speleothem flowstone bracketing (>80–100 ka) vs direct AMS radiocarbon tests on some Holocene/Late Pleistocene Fuyan elements.
evidence.summary: Karst caves in Hunan and Guangxi preserve anatomically modern teeth and mandibles central to active research into whether pre-60 ka Homo sapiens dispersals reached southern China prior to the main Eurasian radiation.
evidence.limits: Karst cave water erosion creates potential mixing requiring direct dating of teeth versus overlying flowstones.

evidence.title: Nwya Devu (Central Tibetan Plateau, 4,600 m): High-altitude prismatic blade workshop
evidence.dateBasis: OSL luminescence and AMS radiocarbon dating across >3,600 stratified slate blades, cores and points on an ancient lakeshore at 4,600 metres elevation.
evidence.summary: Establishes the world’s earliest securely dated high-altitude Upper Paleolithic adaptation on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau roof, following earlier Xiahe Denisovan presence.
evidence.limits: No human skeletons have been excavated directly from the Nwya Devu black-slate workshop horizons.

evidence.title: Xianrendong & Yuchanyan Caves (South China): 20,000-year-old LGM hunter-gatherer pottery
evidence.dateBasis: Direct Bayesian radiocarbon dating on charcoal, animal bone collagen and soot/organic-tempered coarse sherds in Jiangxi and Hunan caves.
evidence.summary: Produced the world’s earliest confirmed fired-clay cooking pots during the cold Last Glacial Maximum by mobile hunter-foragers boiling wild snails, rice grasses, bone grease and acorns long before plant domestication.
evidence.limits: Early limestone cave contexts require cautious screening against old-carbon carbonate reservoir offsets.

evidence.title: Jeongok-ri & Suyanggae (Korean Peninsula): East Asian handaxes & tanged points
evidence.dateBasis: Basalt-tephra OSL dating in the Hantan–Imjin River terraces paired with Upper Paleolithic Suyanggae microblade and stemmed-point radiocarbon sequences.
evidence.summary: Challenged the rigid Movius Line by documenting heavy quartzite handaxes and cleavers at Jeongok-ri (~300–200 ka), succeeded in the Upper Paleolithic by Suyanggae stemmed points, stone engravings and maritime East Sea lithic corridors.
evidence.limits: Acidic Korean peninsula granitic soils destroy almost all Pleistocene organic fauna and skeletal remains outside limestone caves.

evidence.title: Kami-Shirataki, Shiraho-Saonetabaru (Ryukyu) & Odai Yamamoto I (Japan): Obsidian & Incipient Jōmon
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on Ryukyu Pleistocene skeletons (27–20 ka), Hokkaido Shirataki obsidian-blade quarries and charred soot on ~14,500 BCE Odai Yamamoto I pottery.
evidence.summary: Traces Paleolithic island crossings into the Ryukyus (~35 ka), edge-ground axes, long-distance obsidian watercraft exchange from Kozushima Island, and northern Japan’s Late Glacial Odai Yamamoto I pottery.
evidence.limits: Rapid sea-level rise drowned coastal Pleistocene camp belts connecting Kyushu, Honshu and continental shelves.

evidence.title: Sangiran Dome & Trinil (Java, Indonesia): 1.5–0.5 Ma Javanese Homo erectus sequence
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar volcanic tuff and U-Pb/fission-track zircon chronology calibrating >100 Sangiran Homo erectus fossils and shell engraving at Trinil.
evidence.summary: Preserves the richest Early-to-Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus fossil concentration outside Africa across emergent Sundaland floodplains and volcanic lakes of the Solo Basin.
evidence.limits: Refined debates between long (~1.5 Ma) and younger (~1.3 Ma) first-appearance horizons turn on reworked fluvial pumice clasts.

evidence.title: Kalinga (Cagayan Valley, Northern Luzon, Philippines): 709 ka cross-sea hominin presence
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series and 40Ar/39Ar dating of clay-silt beds enveloping an articulated butchered Rhinoceros philippinensis skeleton and 57 stone artefacts.
evidence.summary: Establishes that archaic hominins crossed open ocean channels beyond Wallace’s Line to reach northern Luzon ~709,000 years ago, far earlier than classic island-dwarf Homo luzonensis fossils at Callao Cave.
evidence.limits: No hominin bones occur in the 709 ka Kalinga rhino bed itself.

evidence.title: Niah Great Cave & Gua Dagang (Sarawak, Borneo): Rainforest foraging & “Deep Skull”
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/U-series redating of the West Mouth “Deep Skull” (~45–39 ka), botanical starch residues and Gua Dagang rainforest teeth.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates early Sundaland modern humans managing tropical cave environments with toxic yam detoxification, seasonal pig trapping, fire management and archaic-tooth diversity nearby at Trader’s Cave.
evidence.limits: Early 1950s Harrisson trench units required modern high-precision micro-stratigraphic re-dating.

evidence.title: Leang Karampuang, Leang Tedongnge & Maros-Pangkep Karst (Sulawesi): >51 ka cave art
evidence.dateBasis: Laser-ablation uranium-series dating of calcite “cave popcorn” crusts over figurative warty pig, anoa and human-animal composite narrative scenes.
evidence.summary: Contains the oldest currently dated figurative narrative paintings in the world (>51.2 ka at Leang Karampuang and >45.5 ka at Leang Tedongnge), created by early Wallacean seafarers alongside Leang Burung 2 stone toolkits.
evidence.limits: Laser U-series provides minimum ages from calcite drapes while pigment binders themselves lack datable organic carbon.

evidence.title: Laili & Jerimalai Caves (Timor-Leste, Wallacea): 44 ka pelagic tuna & shell fishhooks
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on marine shell beads, Trochus fishhooks and deep-sea tuna/turtle middens along Timor’s northern limestone terraces.
evidence.summary: On the final southern island stepping-stone toward Australia, Pleistocene mariners caught deep-water pelagic tuna, manufactured shell fishhooks (>16–23 ka) and relied on marine shellfish as glacial aridity stressed terrestrial protein.
evidence.limits: Early 44 ka terrestrial basal layers reflect steep submarine drop-offs that kept Pleistocene beaches close to the caves.

evidence.title: Kosipe & Ivane Valley (Papua New Guinea Highlands, 2,000 m): Waisted axes & montane colonization
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates across volcanic-tephra-interbedded highland swamp valleys yielding waisted stone axes, Pandanus nut char and yam starch.
evidence.summary: Shows rapid adaptive radiation into cold 2,000-metre cloud forests of eastern New Guinea by ~49–44 ka cal BP, clearing canopy gaps with waisted axes and roasting seasonal high-energy Pandanus nuts.
evidence.limits: Acidic highland peat soils consume animal bones, focusing evidence on carbonized nuts and ground/waisted stone tools.

evidence.title: Nawarla Gabarnmang & Kakadu Escarpment (Arnhem Land, Australia): 45 ka pillar gallery & ground axes
evidence.dateBasis: AMS/OSL ceiling and hearth chronologies on pillared sandstone galleries, ground-edge basalt axes and red ochre paintings.
evidence.summary: Alongside nearby Madjedbebe, Jawoyn ancestors engineered sandstone pillar chambers, shaped some of the earliest ground-edge stone hatchets on Earth (>35–45 ka) and painted multistratified ceiling art across Arnhem Land.
evidence.limits: Older edge-ground fragments derive from compressed sandy shelter bases calibrated with single-grain OSL.

evidence.title: Warratyi Rock Shelter (Flinders Ranges, South Australia): Arid-interior settlement ~49 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Combined AMS radiocarbon and single-grain OSL sequences inside an interior arid-zone gorge shelter.
evidence.summary: Proves Homo sapiens penetrated the arid Australian interior more than 2,000 km south of the Arafura coast by ~49–46 ka cal BP, crafting backed artefacts, bone points and red ochre/gypsum pigments alongside giant Diprotodon and Genyornis remains.
evidence.limits: Low sediment volume per spit sparks careful ongoing debate over bone-and-artefact vertical association.

evidence.title: Lake Mungo & Willandra Lakes (NSW, Australia): World’s oldest cremation & red-ochre burial
evidence.dateBasis: OSL dating of lunette dunes enclosing Mungo Lady (WLH 1) and Mungo Man (WLH 3) burials (~42–40 ka) plus ~20 ka fossilized human trackways.
evidence.summary: Records the earliest documented ritual cremation (WLH 1) and red-ochre-dusted inhumation (WLH 3) on Earth, flanked along glacial-era lake dunes by freshwater shell middens and running Pleistocene hunter footprints.
evidence.limits: Erosional blowouts along the Mungo lunette historically exposed burials requiring non-invasive re-burial protocols.

evidence.title: Buang Merabak & Matenkupkum (New Ireland, PNG): Open-ocean Pleistocene Near Oceania
evidence.dateBasis: AMS marine-shell and charcoal dates across coastal limestone caves spanning early crossing of the 100-km channel from New Guinea into New Ireland.
evidence.summary: Documents deliberate blue-water maritime voyaging across oceanic trenches beyond Sahul ~44–40 ka cal BP, followed by purposeful Late Pleistocene translocation of New Britain obsidian and mainland cuscus marsupials.
evidence.limits: Submerged Pleistocene foreshores beneath modern Bismarck reefs conceal additional coastal camps.

evidence.title: Kutikina Cave (Franklin River, Tasmania): Ice Age southernmost hunters at 42.5°S
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated limestone shelter middens with Bennett’s wallaby hunting, Darwin Crater impact-glass transport and quartz thumbnail scrapers.
evidence.summary: During the Bassian Plain glacial land-bridge lowstand, Tasmanian Aboriginal ancestors inhabited sub-alpine river valleys at 42.5°S, collecting bright green meteorite glass from Darwin Crater and creating hand-stencil cave art nearby at Ballawinne.
evidence.limits: Holocene post-glacial rainforest expansion closed cave visibility along remote southwestern gorges.

waves.title: Early Pleistocene Homo erectus Dispersal across Continental & Sunda Asia
waves.summary: Schematic continental and Sundaland corridor marking Early Pleistocene radiations of early Homo / Homo erectus across subtropical and temperate monsoonal Eurasia.
waves.limits: Represents sparse dated locality nodes across a vast timescale rather than a single rapid migration wave.

waves.title: Maritime Crossings of Wallacea & Peopling of Sahul and Near Oceania
waves.dateBasis: Matches Tam Pà Ling, Maros-Pangkep, Laili, Madjedbebe, Kosipe and Buang Merabak chronologies alongside Sahul mitogenome analyses.
waves.summary: Schematic sea-and-island voyaging corridor linking Sunda rainforests across Wallacean deep-water straits to Northern Australia, montane New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago.
waves.limits: Submerged Sunda/Sahul shelves hide initial departure shorelines.

waves.title: Steppe–Siberian & East Asian Upper Paleolithic Expansion to the Arctic and Japan
waves.dateBasis: Combines Ust’-Ishim, Denisova, Mal’ta, Afontova Gora, Yana RHS and Hokkaido/Ryukyu genomic and blade-core datasets.
waves.summary: Schematic northern Eurasian expansion linking Western Siberia, the Altai, Lake Baikal and High Arctic mammoth hunters with Northeast Asian blade and early-pottery groups.
waves.limits: Multiple distinct genetic ancestries (Ancient North Eurasians and East Asian clades) interacted regionally across these routes.
